findings.title: All-client permission is skipped once a per-client resource exists
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) evaluates the all-clients resource only when no resource exists for that client. If any per-client resource exists, for example a VIEW or CONFIGURE permission for that client, the type-level Clients resource is not evaluated. The per-client checks canManage(ClientModel), canConfigure(ClientModel), canMapRoles(ClientModel), canMapCompositeRoles(ClientModel), and canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) all rely on this method, so a caller with a valid MANAGE/CONFIGURE/MAP_ROLES permission for all clients can be denied for any client that also has some individual permission. Conversely, a negative type-level Clients policy is not considered for such clients, which can allow an action that the all-clients policy was intended to deny. The all-clients resource should always be evaluated together with any individual client resource.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission cannot return per-client resources
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...), but per-client resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource are created with resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()) and never have their type set to CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE. Only the type-level resource named "Clients" has that type. As a result, the method misses all concrete client resources and may return the pseudo-resource "Clients" when a type-level permission exists. Callers that treat the returned set as client IDs will either see no concrete clients or an invalid ID.

findings.title: Client deletion cleanup is gated on the old FGAP feature and has no V2 path
findings.body: registerListener now wraps role/client/group cleanup in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), but the factory methods in the same class choose MgmtPermissionsV2 based on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. When only V2 is enabled, ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent is ignored, so authorization resources created for a deleted client are never removed. If both flags are enabled, management(...).clients() resolves to ClientPermissionsV2 and setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) throws UnsupportedOperationException, so client deletion breaks. Client cleanup needs a V2 implementation rather than being gated on the V1 feature flag.

findings.title: Test mutates shared client name without cleanup
findings.body: testManageOnlyOneClient changes myclient's clientId/name to "somethingNew" via clientResource.update(myclient) and never restores it. Other tests in the same class, such as testConfigureOnlyOneClient and testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient, look up clients with realm.admin().clients().findByClientId("myclient").get(0). If this test runs before them, those lookups return an empty list and the tests fail. Restore the client in a finally block or @AfterEach, or avoid changing the shared fixture.
